why: The inserted binding rule after C7 made the model avoid cutting between a noun/role noun and an immediately following identifying element, so many cut positions shifted away from noun+identifier boundaries toward nearby clause or verb boundaries; that change improved measured cohesion for very short pieces (≤3–7 word bins) but also caused new fragmenting cuts around verbs and in enumerations, producing the mix of many small wins and many short-span losses.
lesson: Keep the noun→identifier binding (it helps short-piece cohesion) but avoid forcing cut shifts that fragment verb phrases or split enumerations — preserve clause-level continuity when relocating cuts.
